items.author: Claude (found running the gates for BL-1352, 2026-10-18)
items.title: lp_pool_harness's L7 old-version row has been red since roads became edges
items.design: SPRINT 55 (found running BL-1352's gates, 2026-10-18; NOT caused by it - that change touches no serialisation and save_roundtrip is green). lp_pool_harness reads 18 pass, 1 fail: 'L7 a v49 stream reads, every nation on the mechanical default'. CAUSE, read in the code rather than guessed: the row FABRICATES an old stream by writing a CURRENT snapshot, truncating the trailing share/space/tax sections, and overwriting the version word with k_world_save_version_pre_lp (49). That worked while the tile RECORD was version-independent. BL-1340 (v53) made it version-dependent - r_tile_v reads a u16 road_edges at the current version and a u8 legacy road_level below it - so a v53 body of bytes labelled v49 desyncs at the first tile and the reader refuses the whole stream. The assertion is therefore failing for a true reason: that stream is not a v49 stream. THE FIX is to produce a REAL old stream the way BL-1340 already does for its own case - world_save.cpp has write_world_snapshot_pre_road_edges / write_world_snapshot_at for exactly this - rather than relabelling bytes, and NOT to relax the row. Worth doing because the row guards a real migration (a pre-LP save must load with every nation on the mechanical share default) and a red row nobody owns is how a gate set rots.

items.author: Claude (found smoke-testing BL-1386, 2026-10-19)
items.title: A press on a single-building tile selects the tile, not the building
items.design: SPRINT 55 (found smoke-testing BL-1386, 2026-10-19). ground_bake.lua is RED on nine assertions, all the same shape: 'a press on a single-building tile selects the building (hit zone kept)' and its off-centre variants at zoom 5 and 10 - every one reporting 'got tile'. SELECTION.md's repeat-click cycle has the building outrank the tile on the FIRST press (BL-575 moved unit above building for the same reason: a thing standing on the ground must be reachable without cycling). A SIBLING ROW (found 2026-10-20 during BL-1353's hover card): lens_one_tier.lua's 'no lens: the first press on a built tile still gives the building' is red too, and its last edit (2026-08-29) predates Ben's 2026-10-13 ruling (BL-1312, a plain-canvas press selects the TILE, never the building). items.author: Claude (found verifying BL-1370/1371, 2026-10-17)
items.title: construction_ledger_tabs dies in staging: its fixture is refused for want of a road, not for want of funds
items.design: SPRINT 55 (found verifying BL-1370/1371 on main, 2026-10-17). scripts/verify/construction_ledger_tabs.lua exits 1 with ZERO assertions run - it dies in base.stage_ui_fixture (lib.lua:340, raised at :223) with 'fixture could not place a military base near the player's works: insufficient_funds'. The fixture runs up to 20 verify.econ_step(1) waiting out tech_locked and then places; the corp cannot pay by then. The delivering lane flagged it rather than claiming it pre-existing, which was right, and I could not attribute it either without a build at an older commit. CANDIDATES, in order: (1) BL-1335 taxes, merged the day before, now charge a share of operating profit every quarter the fixture steps - though the tax is floored at 0 so a loss-making fixture corp should pay nothing, which is the first thing to check; (2) the construction rate work changed what a build charges per tick; (3) market prices moved under the fixture so the base simply costs more. NOT a defect in the road or grid work: construction_progress (910), tile_card (71) and roads (31) all pass on the same build with zero failures. THE WORK: find which, then either fix the cause or fund the fixture honestly - never by widening the loop count, which would hide a real cost change. CORRECTED 2026-10-18, and MY FILED PREMISE WAS WRONG. The refusal is not affordability: once verify_api stopped collapsing refusals into 'failed' (see below), the message reads 'fixture could not place a military base near the player's works: needs_road' (lib.lua:249). It is the same BL-1347 gate, reached through place_near_player, which walks up to a 24-ring and is refused needs_road on every tile - so the three candidates I listed (taxes, construction rate, market prices) were all wrong, and the insufficient_funds text I quoted came from the collapsed enum, not from the treasury. THE SHAPE OF THE FIX IS A REAL DECISION, not a one-liner: roading every candidate before trying it would stamp about 2400 crossings, so the honest form is road-on-demand - try build_at, and only on needs_road road THAT tile and retry - which is correct ONLY IF needs_road is the LAST refusal can_place_in_world returns (otherwise a tile refused for the stack or the ceiling gets a road it never needed). Check that ordering first. It reaches about 20 scripts through stage_ui_fixture, so measure what roading each fixture switches on (reach discounts, and in one case the power-wire path) rather than assuming the placement is the only effect. RULED (Ben, 2026-10-18): CHECK THE ORDERING FIRST, then road-on-demand. Confirm needs_road is the LAST refusal can_place_in_world returns before building the retry, so a tile refused for a full stack or a full province ceiling never gets a road it did not need; if the ordering does not hold, fix the ordering or pick a different shape, and say which. Then road only the tile that was actually refused, never the whole candidate ring (about 2400 crossings). verify.stage_road exists for this and Ben granted its report of whether the write landed the same day. ID MOVED on integration, 2026-10-19: filed as BL-1374 in sprint 55's session while sprint 56's worktree filed a different BL-1374 (ZOOM_STAND_INS) at the same time. Sprint 56's keeps the id; this row is the same work under BL-1392. The same collision moved sprint 55's road-halves item to BL-1390 - two in one merge, because next_id.js cannot see an unmerged branch's store.

items.author: Claude (found delivering BL-1347/1348/1357, 2026-10-18)
items.title: The verify world can hold a building on a roadless tile, because its roster is stamped after generation lays site roads
items.design: SPRINT 55 (found delivering BL-1347, 2026-10-18). PRODUCTION.md rules that no building may stand on a tile with no road, and generation now lays a Track to every site it stamps (lay_site_roads, called from make_hard_coded_world and again in finish_campaign_world). But verify_lay_roster is a THIRD stamper - it lays the roster or charter web AFTER generation's pass - so the --verify world can hold a roadless site, which is the one world where the rule does not hold. Measured there: 346 site tiles, 131 unroaded, 130 joinable, 1 unreachable, 135 crossings - so wiring it costs almost nothing. The delivering lane tried it and its run stalled in roads.lua's first wide capture past 5 GB; it then reproduced the SAME stall twice with the call removed, on a machine that had just run two 16-shard sweeps and where wc -l itself timed out, so the stall is UNATTRIBUTED and not evidence against the pass. A comment at verify_api.cpp ~871 carries that finding. THE WORK: wire the pass after verify_lay_roster, then re-run roads.lua on an idle machine - and note that the 40/40 currently recorded for roads.lua came from an earlier run of the same logic, not a fresh one. ID MOVED on integration, 2026-10-19: filed as BL-1377 in sprint 55's session while sprint 56's worktree filed a different BL-1377 (GROUND_UNDER_SIX_GB) at the same time. Sprint 56's keeps the id; this row is the same work under BL-1393. The same collision moved sprint 55's road-halves item to BL-1390 - two in one merge, because next_id.js cannot see an unmerged branch's store.

items.author: Ben (live click on BL-1379, 2026-10-18)
items.title: A newly built road reads as connected in every direction, though the build is pairwise
items.design: SPRINT 55. BEN, in play on 2026-10-18: "It looks like roads are still rendered as adjoining even if the build is pairwise. When I build a new road tile, I see it connect in all possible directions, not just the direction it was built in." WHAT THE CODE SAYS, read the same day: the simulation is right - construction.cpp's lay_road_edge raises ONE crossing (both halves of that one edge), and BOTH draw paths gate on the edge mask, not on the neighbour: body_surface_canvas's draw_network skips a direction where road_tier_on_side is 0 ('nothing is laid across THIS boundary'), and the bake's road_links_of does the same before tile_pieces. So the all-directions read is NOT the two paths disagreeing with the mask, and three candidate causes remain, in order of likelihood: (1) the ARMED HIGHLIGHT persists after the lay, so the legal crossings still drawn around the new tile read as built road (BL-1370's highlight, drawn by the same press); (2) the NEIGHBOUR already carried generated edges on its other sides, so the junction genuinely connects several ways and only the new edge is new; (3) a stale bake chunk re-derived from road rather than road_sides. THE WORK: reproduce live at the zoom Ben was at, name which of the three it is, and fix that one - it is a visual triage item, so the live look comes before any code. It matters beyond itself because BL-1353's lens honesty rests on the road picture being true. ID MOVED on integration, 2026-10-19: filed as BL-1382 in sprint 55's session while sprint 56's worktree filed a different BL-1382 (PROVINCE_NORMALISING_PASS) at the same time. Sprint 56's keeps the id; this row is the same work under BL-1394. The same collision moved sprint 55's road-halves item to BL-1390 - two in one merge, because next_id.js cannot see an unmerged branch's store.

items.author: main session
items.title: Fronts: a neighbour with no free key tile has no front; unreachable front marches retry every tick
items.design: Two edge cases from the BL-1427 (fronts) cold review. (1) Keys are unique per nation and claimed smallest span first, so a span whose every tile another front already claimed has no key and is dropped: a nation touching B only at one tile it also shares with A has no front toward B, against "Every neighbour has fronts" (MILITARY.md § Fronts). 0 cases on the generated world; fronts_harness F1g fails if a seed hits one. Fix by naming a front by (neighbour, tile) or a tie rule that never leaves a span unnamed. (2) A front march the game refuses (the slot or push target on another landmass) is re-issued every tick, re-pathing the province each time; the rival scorer assigns idle units with no reachability check. Assign only to fronts the unit can reach, or stop re-issuing a refused march.

items.author: main session (cold review of BL-1434/BL-1446)
items.title: Hire and refit check goods by price as well as quantity; the PNG inflate gets an output cap
items.design: Cold review of unit designs, 2026-10-28. (1) HIGH, latent until later kit unlocks (BL-1436): hire_goods_affordable counts shelf quantity only, while buy_from_corp_shelves charges the posted price capped by purse_room_of, and debit_kit_goods ignores how much it bought. A design refit (0 credits) with a committed treasury gets its kit free; a hire at exact room drops the treasury below its commitments. The row-goods leg had the flaw already. Fix: the affordability check sums qty x posted price plus the credit cost against purse_room_of, and apply asserts the bought amount. (2) LOW: hire_goods_affordable prices each row axis at its first candidate without the kit draw on the same resource, so an affordable hire can be refused. (3) LOW: png_decode.cpp inflate has no output cap; stop once out exceeds h x (stride+1). (4) LOW: the refit menu labels a design refit with the row gate (+ kit) and omits the changed slots goods; an obsolete own row moves the (live design) entry to the end.
